historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 base growth: H1 FY2026 +15.9% (Q1 +17%) decelerating into tough H2 comps (H2 FY2025 grew ~28%), so FY2026E ~14% and TTM-Jun-2027 vs TTM-Jun-2026 ~13%. The equity CAGR (8.9%) is NOT used as the growth anchor: shareholders' equity is dominated by the 2020 IPO cash, so its compounding tracks retained earnings on a 60bn base, not the operating business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.9% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 30.5% (>30% divergence). Cause: equity is ~RMB60bn of mostly IPO proceeds; FY2020-21 were loss-making on IPO-related SBC. EPS CAGRs are reported but not meaningful (FY2022 base EPS of RMB0.12 after losses in FY2019-21).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF is reported FCF less SBC less interest received (cash basis). Owner 5yr CAGR 19.6% vs reported 22.3%: the gap is interest income growing with the cash pile (115m FY2020 -> 1,682m FY2025), not SBC, which fell. The 3-year owner CAGR (97%) is distorted at both ends -- FY2022 carried a one-off RMB2.23bn intangible-asset purchase in capex and FY2025 a RMB3.6bn working-capital inflow -- and should not be read as a trend. FY2021 owner FCF was negative because IPO-related SBC (2.58bn) exceeded cash generation.

scenario_narratives.base: JD Health keeps compounding as China's largest online pharmacy, with revenue growth easing from ~13% toward 3.5% over a decade as online penetration of pharmaceutical retail matures and the 2026 prescription-drug rules take some edge off AI-assisted conversion without breaking the model. The axes that matter are (1) services mix -- marketplace, advertising and insurance-payment facilitation growing faster than 1P merchandise, lifting gross margin from 25% toward 28%; (2) fulfilment leverage from JD Logistics and the 450-store omnichannel network; and (3) the cash tax rate normalising toward 20% as offshore-exempt finance income shrinks in the mix. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin matures at 10.5%, giving an owner-FCF margin of ~8%. The RMB71.5bn cash pile is taken at face value in the bridge; whether minority holders ever see it (buybacks only restarted in H1 FY2026 at RMB846m) is the real debate, and it is why the stock trades at ~5x owner FCF ex-cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'first online marketplace for new drug launches' positioning turns into a durable procurement moat: innovative-drug exclusives, medical-insurance online payment in 40+ cities and on-demand delivery keep growth in the mid-teens through 2029, services reach a quarter of revenue, and the margin ramp seen in H1 FY2026 (non-IFRS operating margin 7.0% -> 8.5%) continues to a 13% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Policy tailwinds (health-consumption and AI+healthcare plans in the 15th Five-Year Plan) favour the compliant scale incumbent. The company steps up buybacks or dividends from the cash pile, closing the discount the market applies to cash controlled by JD.com.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulation and competition bite together. The NMPA compliance guidelines slow Rx order growth and ban the AI-assistant workflows JD Health has been building; Alibaba Health and Meituan on-demand pharmacy compete on price and delivery speed; JD.com's connected-transaction terms (3% of fulfilled-order value through 2028) leave little room to defend margin. Revenue growth falls to high single digits immediately and to ~3% by mid-decade, the pre-SBC EBITDA margin stalls at 7-8%, preferential tax rates lapse, and the cash earns less as PRC rates fall. Even here the cash pile covers ~70% of the current share price, so the bear case is a value-trap outcome -- a cash-rich business whose cash is never returned -- rather than a capital-loss outcome on the fundamentals.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC fully expensed and the share count held flat; interest income stripped and the entire RMB71.5bn of cash resources (cash, term deposits, bank wealth-management products) added back once in the bridge at book/fair value. Ten-year explicit horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping at year 5. Discounted at a single CNY-built 10% in every scenario; risk lives in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights. Per-share values are computed in RMB and converted to HKD at the dated 1.1759 rate, parity-checked against the RMB counter.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash pile realisation: RMB22.3/share (HK$26.2) of the value is cash resources controlled by a 68% shareholder; the model takes it at face. A permanent 20% market discount on that cash is worth ~HK$5/share.

Working-capital float: ~RMB12bn of the cash is supplier-funded (payables + accruals exceed inventories + receivables); it is real as long as revenue does not shrink, and the model's positive wc_capture assumes the payables ratio holds as revenue grows.

Regulatory: the May-2026 NMPA online prescription-drug rules directly target AI-assisted prescription workflows and Rx promotion; a harder enforcement path than the base assumes moves year-1 growth from 13% toward the bear's 8%.

Margin maturity: the base 10.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin is above any full year printed (6.4% FY2025, 9.0% H1 FY2026 half-year); the terminal value is ~55-60% of EV, so each 1pp of mature margin is worth roughly HK$6-7/share.
Currency: the HKD value moves one-for-one with HKD/CNY; the 1.1759 rate is dated 2026-10-23 and is not refreshed by refresh_price.py.

Related-party terms: technology/traffic, logistics and payment services from JD.com at 3% of fulfilled-order value are fixed to 2028; a reset on renewal is a direct margin lever outside JD Health's control.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular HKEX close); 52-week range 31.84-71.70 HKD. FX from Yahoo HKDCNY=X the same day, parity-checked against the 86618.HK RMB counter.
data_sources.financials: 6618.HK_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (TermDeposits, InterestIncome, CashTaxesPaid, ShareRepurchases, Depreciation, MerchandiseSalesRevenue, ServicesRevenue); FY2025 annual report (income statement, cash-flow statement, note 9 tax reconciliation, note 32(a) working-capital reconciliation, non-IFRS reconciliation); H1 FY2026 interim report (statement of financial position, cash-flow statement, notes 9-11, non-IFRS reconciliation).
data_sources.qualitative: 6618.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-24): business model, moat factors, regulatory risk register, bull/bear cases, H1 FY2026 and FY2025 management commentary.

inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 2026-06-30: FY2025 73,441.5 + H1 FY2026 40,887.9 - H1 FY2025 35,290.0. FY0 is a TTM so the flows share the June-2026 balance-sheet date; year 1 is the twelve months to June 2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: H1 FY2026 interim note 9 diluted weighted-average (3,177.6m basic + 26.7m dilutive options/RSUs). Shares in issue 3,211.1m at 2026-06-30 before treasury shares (RMB757.7m, ~18-25m shares repurchased pending cancellation plus scheme-trust shares). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it.
inputs.cash_composition_note: RMB m at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 interim, statement of financial position + notes 10/11): cash & equivalents 20,445.6 + restricted cash 6.8 + term deposits 13,726.1 + bank wealth-management products at FVTPL 34,084.7 (20,840.6 non-current + 13,244.1 current; expected 1.55-4.90% p.a.) + wealth-management products at amortised cost 3,233.6 (1,376.1 non-current + 1,857.5 current; 4.20-5.53% p.a.) = 71,496.8, which ties to the company's own 'cash resources of RMB71.5 billion'. Equity investments in private companies (94.1) excluded. No borrowings. Lease liabilities (874.9) excluded from net debt under lease treatment (B). FY2025 tax reconciliation shows RMB559m of tax effect from tax-exempt entities (~RMB2.2bn of profit at 25%), i.e. substantially all finance income is earned offshore -- no PRC withholding-tax haircut applied. Per share this pile is RMB22.3 / HK$26.2, roughly 70% of the current price at inputs.price_as_of: the market is paying ~HK$11 per share, ~5x owner FCF, for the operating business.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 2026-06-30: OCF 8,390.2 (10,173.9 + 4,461.0 - 6,244.7) less capex 205.4 (151.0 + 90.5 - 36.1). FY2025 OCF alone was 10,173.9 but included a 3,601m working-capital inflow (trade payables +2,792, accruals +1,932, inventories -1,025); that is why the forward FCF is built from components with a working-capital capture on revenue CHANGE rather than carried forward.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received on the cash-flow statement, TTM: 1,682.1 + 775.5 - 782.9. Stripped because the entire cash pile is added to EV. Fair-value gains on FVTPL wealth-management products never enter OCF (reversed in the note 32(a) reconciliation; realised in investing), so no further adjustment is needed.
inputs.sbc_source: Non-IFRS reconciliation, FY2025 annual report p.26 (590,724) and H1 FY2026 interim report (309,110; H1 FY2025 355,441); ties to the cash-flow add-back. No separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis); net-share settlement is not used, options are exercised for cash.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 FY2026 financing outflow 'payments and prepayments for repurchase of ordinary shares' 845,777 (RMB'000); nil in FY2024 and FY2025. The flat count is therefore now being funded, at roughly 1.5x the SBC run-rate.
inputs.fx_note: HKD per CNY = 1 / 0.8504 (Yahoo HKDCNY=X, 2026-10-23). Statements, flows and the DCF are in RMB; the HKEX quote is HKD. Parity check against the RMB counter 86618.HK on 2026-10-23: the HKD close at inputs.price_as_of x 0.8504 reproduces the observed RMB-counter close within 0.1%, which fixes the rate, the direction and the quote basis. Every per-share value is computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1759 for the HKD quote basis. The rate is dated; refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T08:08:08Z (16:08 HKT, regular close incl. closing auction; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8% + China equity risk premium incl. country risk ~6.5% x beta ~1.2 for an HK-listed China internet platform = ~9.6%, rounded up to 10.0% for the governance discount (JD.com controls ~68% and the VIE/Cayman structure governs minority holders' claim on the offshore cash) -- that is a claim-on-cash-flows risk, not a flows risk, so it belongs in the rate. Zero debt, so WACC = cost of equity. The SAME 10% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, competition and the May-2026 prescription-drug rules are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (FY2025 68.1 + 11.1; H1 FY2026 56.2 + 8.7; TTM 113.8, ~0.15% of revenue and rising with the 450-store JD Pharmacy rollout) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (609.2 non-current + 265.7 current) EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct is set ex right-of-use depreciation (~0.25% vs 0.35% total D&A) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are nil at 2026-06-30 (RMB1.4m at FY2025, loss-making); flows are treated as 100% attributable with no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: consumer-internet / 1P pharmacy e-commerce marketplace, HK-listed, RMB filer) routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 with the non-US adaptations (dual currency, IFRS-16 leases, matching-asset rule for the cash pile). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry. EBITDA margin is calibrated to the company's own non-IFRS operating income (GP - opex + SBC - financial-asset impairments; 8.5% H1 FY2026, 7.0% H1 FY2025, 6.0% FY2025) plus D&A: pre-SBC EBITDA margin 6.4% FY2025, 9.0% H1 FY2026, 7.3% TTM. H2 is seasonally weaker (Double-11 promotions; H2 FY2025 non-IFRS operating margin ~5.0%). Working capital: a 1P retailer with payables + accruals (20.2bn) well above inventories + receivables (7.9bn) -- a negative-working-capital model where growth GENERATES cash, so wc_capture_pct is positive (FY2025 23.6% of the revenue increase, FY2024 11.3%; structural ratio ~16%); base uses 12%. Interest income is deducted from last_fcf and the whole cash pile sits in the bridge at book/fair value. SBC has fallen from 8.4% of revenue (FY2021, IPO grants) to 0.7% TTM and is projected to drift only to 0.6%, not lower. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (section 1 of owner-fcf.md) and are recorded for information only.

bear.rationale: The May-2026 NMPA prescription-drug rules (no AI-assisted prescription review, mandatory pharmacist checks, no promotional inducements, stricter identity checks) cut Rx conversion and raise compliance cost; Alibaba Health and Meituan/Ele.me on-demand compete on price; growth falls to high single digits in year 1 and to GDP-like rates by year 5. Margin is roughly flat at 7-8% pre-SBC as compliance and pharmacist staffing absorb the mix gains; SBC stays at 0.8% as retention grants replace the lapsed IPO awards; preferential tax rates lapse (22%). Lower wc_capture because slower growth builds less supplier float; terminal cap 15x for a business growing at nominal GDP.

base.rationale: Growth decelerates from the H1 FY2026 run-rate as online pharmacy penetration matures and the new Rx rules slow order growth; EBITDA margin climbs ~0.3-0.5pp a year on services mix (services +34% vs merchandise +25% in FY2025) and fulfilment leverage, maturing at 10.5% pre-SBC (vs 9.0% in H1 FY2026, 7.3% TTM) -- below the H1 run-rate annualised because H2 is structurally weaker. Cash tax ramps 16% -> 20%: FY2025 book ETR was 11% only because offshore finance income is tax-exempt; on operating profit the rate is ~18%, and HNTE 15% preferences and withholding on repatriation push it toward 20% over time. Terminal growth 3.0% nominal RMB (below China nominal GDP); cap 18x owner FCF.

bull.rationale: Growth holds in the mid-teens for three years on new-drug-launch exclusives (100+ in FY2025, 65 in H1 FY2026), medical-insurance online payment scaling past 40 cities, and on-demand pharmacy; services revenue reaches ~25% of the mix and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 13% (still below Alibaba Health's marketplace-heavy peers' aspiration but above anything JD Health has printed). Capex slightly higher for the offline pharmacy footprint. Higher wc_capture because faster growth means faster payables build.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because there is a live single-regulator trigger (the May-2026 NMPA prescription-drug rules, rated high severity in the Analysis) and a high-severity competitive axis, and because the investment case leans on a cash pile the controlling shareholder has only just begun to return. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold -- mid-teens growth for several more years despite tougher comps, margins nearly doubling from the FY2025 level, and a change in capital-return policy. Base 50%: the H1 FY2026 print (revenue +15.9%, non-IFRS operating margin +1.5pp) is squarely on the base path.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
